sections.html:
Four steps: a cashier checks it, a barcode goes on every page, it is scanned, and the details are keyed into the index. The Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg runs the routine for speed.

At the counter the cashier confirms the paper is an original, properly signed, dated and acknowledged before a notary whose seal, signature and commission expiration date appear. Fees and transfer taxes are collected right then. A 15-digit number is assigned, and a sticker on each page shows the page count, the amount paid and the date and time of recording. After scanning, the document goes back to whoever filed it, in person or by mail. Data entry staff finish the index from the legal description, and a second team double-checks it.

Westmoreland is one of only two counties in Pennsylvania where deeds are recorded and returned right away, with no wait of a day or two. For a seller that means the new owner's name reaches the public record on closing day. Offices keep hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays and close on the county holiday calendar.

The office offers a free guide to searching records by name, instrument number, document category, municipality, subdivision or lot. Searches by tax map number or UPI also work, though only where the original document listed one.

A deed or a mortgage costs $110.25 to record. Every listed document includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI, and the office asks for exact payment with anything mailed in.

Westmoreland County recording fees
Document or add-onFee
Deed$110.25
Mortgage$110.25
Re-recorded deed or mortgage$112.25
Mortgage satisfaction or release$84.25
Easement or right of way$82.25
Power of attorney$41.00
Extra name$0.50
Extra page$2.00
Extra UPI$20.00

Questions about any charge go to 724-830-3518 or ROD@westmorelandcountypa.gov. Pay with cash, a money order, a cashier's or certified check, or a personal check with ID. Debit and credit cards are not accepted. When you send several documents, one check can cover no more than five, so each document after the fifth needs its own.

The PIN is the parcel identifier number, and Westmoreland County requires it on every document it records. It is a 10-digit number whose first digits point to the district, the map page and the lot.

A deed with a missing or wrong number is one of the quickest ways to get a closing package returned. If you cannot find the number on a tax bill, ask the Tax Assessment Office at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue, Suite 440, Greensburg, or search the online record index. The index can be searched by name or by instrument number, and for anything recorded before November 13, 2000, by book and page.

Tax map numbers were not required until 2009, so older documents may not turn up in a search by map number.

Open an account with SimpliFile or CSC and upload the scanned original. Each vendor has its own sign-up steps, so read them first.

Documents sent this way go first to the county's UPI and GIS Tax Mapping department for review, then on to the recorder once certified. Nearly every document type qualifies, with one exception: anything with an attachment to the Statement of Value must come by mail or in person. An e-recorded attachment would add to the page count, and the office cannot alter the page count, so you would pay for pages that cost nothing when handed over the counter.

  • Mailed recordings and requests need stamped, self-addressed envelopes.
  • Include a phone number with your paperwork.
  • Plans must have original signatures, and the 18 by 24 inch plan fee is $49.00 for the first page and $20.00 for each page after that.

Send either the tax itself or a Statement of Value. Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state realty transfer tax, and the Department of Revenue holds buyer and seller jointly liable. The recorder collects it, often alongside a local share.

Every deed has to state the true consideration or come with two copies of an Affidavit of Value. A claimed exemption, full or partial, must be backed by that affidavit filed in duplicate, with street addresses, consideration, assessed value, fair market value, mortgages recorded and an explanation of why the transaction is or is not taxable. The affidavit must cite the regulation that supports the exemption.

  • Family transfers are the usual exemption, and the exemption must be stated clearly in the deed.
  • A deed with taxes in more than one municipality must say how the transfer taxes are divided.
  • Ask the office for the Realty Transfer Tax Rates sheet, since rates differ by municipality.

sections.h2: Westmoreland County housing at a glance
sections.html: This Pittsburgh-area county has about 349,324 residents, 169,961 housing units and 154,979 households, and 78.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is worth $203,500 and median gross rent is $879. Population has slipped 1.5 percent since the 2020 count of 354,663. A Land Bank and Development Authority works on vacant, abandoned and tax-delinquent properties, a sign that older neighborhoods vary a great deal from street to street.

sections.h2: From closing to a returned deed
sections.html:
Because Westmoreland returns documents right away, a seller whose deed is filed in person can leave with the recorded original and its sticker, or have it mailed back. Include a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want it by mail, and put a phone number in the package so staff can reach you about a problem.

Before closing, have your title company confirm four things: the PIN, the number of pages and names for the fee table, the transfer tax or Affidavit of Value, and whether the file goes electronically or on paper. A cash sale skips the lender documents, but the recorder asks for the same items either way.

If a document is rejected, ask staff which item failed. The usual culprits are a notary block missing its seal or commission expiration date, a wrong or absent PIN, a fee total that is off, and a Statement of Value attachment sent electronically. Fix the item and refile, and keep the receipt sticker information for your records. Ask staff for a total before you resubmit so the fee is exact the second time.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Westmoreland County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $110.25, which includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI. Extra names cost $0.50, extra pages $2.00 and extra UPIs $20.00. Realty transfer tax is collected separately.

faqs.q: Does the Westmoreland County recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: No. Accepted payments are cash, money orders, cashier's or certified checks and personal checks, and debit and credit cards are refused. In person, a personal check needs a valid photo ID and the signer must be present.

faqs.q: Can I e-record every document in Westmoreland County?
faqs.a: Almost all of them. The one exception is a document with an attachment to the Statement of Value, which must be mailed or brought in. Use SimpliFile or CSC for everything else.

faqs.q: What happens if I send several documents in one envelope?
faqs.a: One check can cover no more than five documents. Enclose a separate check for each document beyond the first five, plus a stamped, self-addressed return envelope.

faqs.q: Is a PIN required on a Westmoreland County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. A 10-digit parcel identifier number is required on all documents, in addition to the usual acknowledgment and notary details. Ask the Tax Assessment Office if you cannot find it.
